answer: A mesa-shaped trust curve resists sybils: a new agent starts on the flat base with tiny transaction caps and can only climb toward the zenith after months of verified, useful work that other agents genuinely relied on. Each identity must also keep a small ember of stake burning, a deposit slashed if the agent is caught duplicating work or vouching for fake peers. An attacker wanting a hundred fake voices must fund a hundred deposits and fake a hundred long histories, while one honest climb costs almost nothing.
